claims: One repository-owned Python runner executes fixed trusted local and remote CI plans. It loads no command from cards, manifests, ledgers, user strings, shells, or plugin registries. Pull-request and release workflows delegate to its test, docs, and package profiles, while one local command runs the complete plan.

The runner permits unchanged pre-existing local dirt, refuses any change caused by a check, and provides a strict clean-repository mode for remote CI. It uses fresh output locations, runs package probes outside the repository, stops on the first failing stage, and reports actionable stage and purity failures.

Every future CC-R candidate requires one active RED, GREEN, SLICE, DISPROOF, REGRESSION, PACKAGE, and ATTEST result in exact order before eligibility, integration, completion, or selection. RED alone permits EXPECTED_FAILURE; PACKAGE permits only PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE. Stored commands remain evidence and are never executed by CI.

The complete governed run passes changed-boundary Ruff, 1,803 configured tests with 2 skips, 12 separate compiler tests, both governance validators, 40 GraphRecipe tests, strict Sphinx HTML, doctest, and linkcheck, real sdist and wheel checks, isolated installation, and all three package probes.

The KISS correction restores pyproject.toml byte-for-byte and runs future compiler tests through one dedicated nonduplicated stage. The final correction makes the latest-document drift test follow active append-only revision history. GraphRecipe remains green without a canonical report, graph, card, decision, program, or integration-row cascade. Only three new exact FILE ownership reservations are added.

This verification starts or completes no CC-R stage. It changes no compiler semantics, production or runtime behavior, release decision, hook installer, merge protection, API compatibility, public namespace, ontology, dependency, package topology, canonical graph, candidate, selection, or worker ledger.
limitations: The runner supplies a local and remote CI entry point, not proof that an unprotected local merge invoked it. Hook installation and merge-queue policy remain future work.
The scaffold depends on the repository's declared development environment. It does not add ad hoc dependency installation or redefine the governed compiler environment.
This is CC-000 infrastructure evidence only. Each R stage still needs separate authorization, RED and GREEN history, semantic evidence, integration, and attestation.

summary: Verify fixed local CI and strict research TDD enforcement.
why: The retained evidence binds the exact implementation bytes, two-commit correction history, fixed command plans, workflow parity, source-purity guards, ordered research TDD admission, full tests, documentation, package probes, and unchanged GraphRecipe contract. These facts establish reusable CI scaffolding without claiming that any R workstream has begun or widening compiler, runtime, release, API, packaging, hook, or graph authority.
